cover.title:
Trapping
**Rain Water**
cover.promise: You'll solve **LeetCode 42** in O(1) extra space.

slides.title: After the rain
slides.scene: This is Trapping Rain Water, told as a row of brick walls after rain.

blocks.text: Six walls stand side by side, each one brick wide. Heavy rain falls. Water stays in every dip it cannot spill out of.

blocks.label: HOW MANY SQUARES OF WATER STAY?

slides.title: LeetCode 42
slides.lead: Each bar is 1 wide. Return how much water stays trapped after rain.

blocks.text: The walls are the array. Each square of water is 1 unit.

slides.try_first: Draw [3, 0, 1, 4, 0, 2] on paper and count the water first.

slides.teaser: Hint 1: one bar at a time
slides.title: One bar at a time
slides.lead: Forget the whole puddle. Ask each bar: how much water sits right on top of me?

blocks.label: THE SLOW WAY, FOR BAR 1
blocks.note: Scan everything to its left, then everything to its right. Do that for every bar.

blocks.text: Then add up the water on every bar. It works, but n scans of n bars is O(n²).

slides.title: Shorter wall wins
slides.lead: Above a bar, water rises to the tallest wall on each side, then spills over the shorter one.

slides.title: Two walkers
slides.lead: Start one walker at each end, like two pointers in post 06.

blocks.text: Each walker remembers the tallest wall it has passed. Only the shorter side decides the water.

slides.title: Move the lower side
slides.lead: If height[left] < height[right], the left bar's water depends only on leftMax.

blocks.note: 3 is not less than 2, so the right walker settles bar 5 first.

blocks.text: A taller wall waits on the other side, so the lower side's max is the real limit. Settle that bar, then step in.

final.caption: The walkers met. {{TOTAL}} squares of water stay.

slides.title: Set up the walk
slides.lead: Two walkers at the ends, two tallest-wall counters, one total.

after.text: The loop runs until the walkers meet. Every step settles one bar for good.

items.label: Time
items.note: Each step moves one walker inward.

learnt: Two walkers, one at each end
slides.pattern: Two pointers that settle the lower side first.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.note: Same walls, same two walkers, a new question.
